decisions.reason: "사람" already includes men and women, so the English gender span has no Korean counterpart.

decisions.choice: "mọi người" (L), with no gender span (also 12:18)
decisions.reason: "Mọi người" includes men and women; Vietnamese has no traditional masculine form for the setting to offer, as in 3:4.

source.text: εἰ δυνατόν, τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν μετὰ πάντων ἀνθρώπων εἰρηνεύοντες·

records.literal_gloss: If possible, the [part] from you, with all men being at peace;

en.L: If [it is] possible, as far as it depends on you, being at peace with all {{gender:people|men}};
en.B: If it can be done, and so far as it lies with you, keep peace with everyone.
en.R: Do all that you can to live in peace with everyone, if that is possible.

es.L: Si [es] posible, en lo que de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} depende, estando en paz con {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}};
es.B: Si se puede, y hasta donde esté en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} manos, {{plural_you:mantengan|mantened}} la paz con todos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} todo lo que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} por vivir en paz con todos, si es posible.

sw.L: Ikiwezekana, kwa upande wenu, mkiwa na amani na watu wote;
sw.B: Ikiwezekana, na kwa kadiri inavyowategemea ninyi, dumisheni amani na kila mtu.
sw.R: Fanyeni yote mnayoweza ili kuishi kwa amani na kila mtu, ikiwezekana.

fr.L: Si [c’est] possible, autant que cela dépend de vous, étant en paix avec {{gender:tous les êtres humains|tous les hommes}} ;
fr.B: Si c’est possible, et pour autant que cela dépende de vous, vivez en paix avec tout le monde.
fr.R: Faites tout ce que vous pouvez pour vivre en paix avec tout le monde, si c’est possible.

ko.L: 할 수 있다면, 여러분에게 달린 대로 모든 사람과 평화롭게 지내십시오.
ko.B: 할 수 있는 대로, 여러분 쪽에서는 모든 사람과 평화를 이루며 지내십시오.
ko.R: 할 수만 있다면, 여러분이 할 수 있는 모든 것을 다 해서 모든 사람과 평화롭게 사십시오.

vi.L: Nếu có thể, tùy ở phần anh chị em, sống hòa thuận với mọi người;
vi.B: Nếu có thể được, và trong chừng mực tùy thuộc nơi anh chị em, hãy giữ hòa thuận với mọi người.
vi.R: Hãy làm hết sức mình để sống hòa thuận với mọi người, nếu điều đó có thể được.

decisions.choice: two limits: if it can be done, and as far as it depends on you
decisions.reason: "If possible" admits that peace is not always possible. τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν, "the [part] from you", limits the command to the believer's own side: others may refuse peace.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: "평화" for peace with others, as at 3:17
decisions.reason: "평안" is kept for inner peace from God (8:6); peace between people is "평화".

source.text: μὴ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκδικοῦντες, ἀγαπητοί, ἀλλὰ δότε τόπον τῇ ὀργῇ, γέγραπται γάρ· Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, λέγει κύριος.

records.literal_gloss: Not yourselves avenging, beloved, but give place to the wrath, it has been written for: To me vengeance, I will repay, says [the] Lord.

en.L: Not avenging yourselves, beloved, but give place to the wrath, for it is written, "Vengeance [is] mine, I will repay," says [the] Lord.
en.B: Dear friends, never avenge yourselves. Step aside and let God's wrath do its work, for it is written, "Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay," says the Lord.
en.R: My dear friends, do not try to get even with anyone. Leave that to God and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. Scripture tells us that the Lord says, "It is my place to punish. I will pay people back."

es.L: No {{plural_you:vengándose ustedes|vengándoos vosotros}} mismos, amados, sino {{plural_you:den|dad}} lugar a la ira, porque está escrito: «Mía [es] la venganza, yo pagaré», dice [el] Señor.
es.B: Queridos, nunca {{plural_you:tomen|toméis}} venganza por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} cuenta. {{plural_you:Háganse|Haceos}} a un lado y {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que la ira de Dios haga su obra, porque está escrito: «A mí me corresponde la venganza; yo pagaré», dice el Señor.
es.R: Queridos amigos, no {{plural_you:traten de vengarse|tratéis de vengaros}} de nadie. {{plural_you:Déjenselo|Dejádselo}} a Dios y a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira. La Escritura dice que el Señor afirma: «Castigar me corresponde a mí. Yo daré a cada uno lo que merece».

sw.L: Bila kujilipizia kisasi wenyewe, wapendwa, bali ipeni nafasi ghadhabu; kwa maana imeandikwa, "Kisasi ni changu; mimi nitalipa," asema Bwana.
sw.B: Wapendwa, kamwe msijilipizie kisasi. Jiwekeni kando, iachieni ghadhabu ya Mungu ifanye kazi yake, kwa maana imeandikwa, "Kisasi ni changu; mimi nitalipa," asema Bwana.
sw.R: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, msijaribu kulipiza kisasi kwa mtu yeyote. Mwachieni Mungu jambo hilo na ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Maandiko yanatuambia kwamba Bwana anasema, "Ni kazi yangu kuadhibu. Mimi nitawalipa watu."

fr.L: Ne vous vengeant pas vous-mêmes, bien-aimés, mais laissez place à la colère, car il est écrit : « À moi la vengeance, moi je rendrai la pareille », dit [le] Seigneur.
fr.B: Chers amis, ne vous faites jamais justice vous-mêmes. Écartez-vous et laissez la colère de Dieu faire son œuvre, car il est écrit : « C’est à moi qu’appartient la vengeance ; c’est moi qui rendrai à chacun son dû », dit le Seigneur.
fr.R: Mes chers amis, n’essayez pas de vous venger de qui que ce soit. Laissez cela à Dieu et à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère. L’Écriture nous dit que le Seigneur déclare : « C’est à moi de punir. C’est moi qui rendrai à chacun ce qu’il mérite. »

ko.L: 사랑하는 여러분, 스스로 원수를 갚지 말고, 진노에 자리를 내어 주십시오. 기록되었기 때문입니다. "원수 갚는 일은 내게 [속하였으니], 내가 갚겠다. 주께서 말씀하신다."
ko.B: 사랑하는 여러분, 절대로 직접 원수를 갚지 말고, 하나님의 진노에 맡기십시오. 성경에 이렇게 기록되어 있기 때문입니다. "원수를 갚는 것은 내가 할 일이다. 내가 갚아 주겠다. 주께서 말씀하신다."
ko.R: 사랑하는 여러분, 누구에게도 앙갚음하려고 하지 마십시오. 그 일은 하나님께 맡기고, 하나님께서 진노하시도록 하십시오. 성경에서 주님께서 이렇게 말씀하십니다. "벌을 주는 것은 내가 할 일이다. 내가 사람들에게 갚아 주겠다."

vi.L: Đừng tự mình báo thù, thưa những người yêu dấu, nhưng hãy nhường chỗ cho cơn thịnh nộ, vì có chép: "Sự báo thù [thuộc về] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ báo trả", Chúa phán.
vi.B: Thưa anh chị em yêu dấu, đừng bao giờ tự mình báo thù, nhưng hãy lui ra để cơn thịnh nộ của Đức Chúa Trời hành động, vì có lời chép: "Sự báo thù thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ báo trả", Chúa phán vậy.
vi.R: Anh chị em thân mến, đừng tìm cách trả thù ai. Hãy để việc đó cho Đức Chúa Trời và cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Kinh Thánh cho chúng ta biết Chúa phán: "Trừng phạt là việc của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta sẽ báo trả cho người ta."

decisions.choice: give place to the wrath: leave room for God's wrath, his judgment
alternatives: make room for your enemy's anger, without answering it
give your own anger time to cool
decisions.reason: Romans uses ὀργή with the article for God's wrath (2:5, 3:5, 5:9), and the quotation that follows says that vengeance belongs to God. So the wrath is God's: leave judgment to him.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 32:35
decisions.reason: The quotation is from Deuteronomy 32:35, closer to the Hebrew than to the old Greek translation; Hebrews 10:30 quotes it in the same form. In Deuteronomy the speaker is the LORD, named with the divine name in the surrounding verses (32:36). "Says the Lord" is Paul's addition, a common prophetic formula; the Greek has the word for Lord.

decisions.choice: dear friends
decisions.reason: As at Philippians 4:1: "beloved" is church language.

decisions.choice: God's wrath / God and his anger
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: for it is written (L, B); Scripture says (R)
decisions.reason: The normal formula for quoting Scripture; Readable names Scripture, as at 1:17.

decisions.choice: Chers amis (B); Mes chers amis (R); bien-aimés (L)
decisions.reason: The word means people Paul loves. "Bien-aimés" is kept at Literal; as a form of address it now sounds like church language, so Balanced and Readable say "chers amis", as the English says "dear friends".

decisions.choice: "사랑하는 여러분" at every level
decisions.reason: The address keeps the letter's 합쇼체 and "여러분".

decisions.choice: "진노에 자리를 내어 주다" (L); "하나님의 진노에 맡기다" (B); "하나님께서 진노하시도록 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The wrath is God's wrath, his judgment (meaning decision, footnoted). Literal keeps the bare "진노" as the Greek does; Balanced and Readable name God, as the English does. "진노" is the letter's word (1:18).

decisions.choice: "주" (L, B), "주님" (R), with no divine_name span; God's words in 해라체
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios, as in the quotations at 10:13 and 11:34.

decisions.choice: "thưa những người yêu dấu" (L); "thưa anh chị em yêu dấu" (B); "anh chị em thân mến" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means beloved, dear ones; it is not "brothers", so it takes no gender span. Balanced and Readable add "anh chị em", the word for the readers through the letter, as a Vietnamese letter would; "hỡi" belongs to older speech (1:13).

decisions.choice: "cơn thịnh nộ" (L) without "of God"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the wrath as God's, with a footnote. Literal keeps the bare noun as the Greek does, with "cơn thịnh nộ", the word kept for God's wrath through the letter (1:18), which already points to God; Balanced and Readable name him.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ἐὰν πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου, ψώμιζε αὐτόν· ἐὰν διψᾷ, πότιζε αὐτόν· τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But if hungers the enemy of you, feed him; if he thirsts, give drink him; this for doing coals of fire you will heap upon the head of him.

en.L: But if your enemy is hungry, feed {{gender:them|him}}; if {{gender:they are|he is}} thirsty, give {{gender:them|him}} drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire on {{gender:their|his}} head.
en.B: Instead, if your enemy is hungry, give {{gender:them|him}} food; if {{gender:they are|he is}} thirsty, give {{gender:them|him}} something to drink. By doing this you will pile burning coals on {{gender:their|his}} head.
en.R: Instead, if your enemy is hungry, give {{gender:them|him}} food. If {{gender:they are|he is}} thirsty, give {{gender:them|him}} something to drink. When you do this, it will be like piling burning coals on {{gender:their|his}} head. Your kindness may make {{gender:them|him}} ashamed and sorry.

es.L: Pero si tu enemigo tiene hambre, dale de comer; si tiene sed, dale de beber; porque haciendo esto amontonarás carbones de fuego sobre su cabeza.
es.B: Al contrario: si tu enemigo tiene hambre, dale algo de comer; si tiene sed, dale algo de beber. Haciendo esto, apilarás brasas encendidas sobre su cabeza.
es.R: Al contrario, si tu enemigo tiene hambre, dale comida. Si tiene sed, dale algo de beber. Cuando haces esto, es como si pusieras brasas encendidas sobre su cabeza. Tu bondad puede hacer que sienta vergüenza y se arrepienta.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa adui yako ana njaa, mlishe; ikiwa ana kiu, mpe kinywaji; kwa maana kwa kufanya hivi utarundika makaa ya moto juu ya kichwa chake.
sw.B: Badala yake, ikiwa adui yako ana njaa, mpe chakula; ikiwa ana kiu, mpe kitu cha kunywa. Kwa kufanya hivyo utarundika makaa yanayowaka juu ya kichwa chake.
sw.R: Badala yake, adui yako akiwa na njaa, mpe chakula. Akiwa na kiu, mpe kitu cha kunywa. Ukifanya hivyo, itakuwa kama kumrundikia makaa yanayowaka kichwani. Wema wako unaweza kumfanya aone aibu na ajute.

fr.L: Mais si ton ennemi a faim, nourris-le ; s’il a soif, donne-lui à boire ; car en faisant cela, tu amasseras des charbons de feu sur sa tête.
fr.B: Au contraire, si ton ennemi a faim, donne-lui de quoi manger ; s’il a soif, donne-lui de quoi boire. En agissant ainsi, tu entasseras des braises sur sa tête.
fr.R: Au contraire, si ton ennemi a faim, donne-lui à manger. S’il a soif, donne-lui à boire. Quand tu fais cela, c’est comme si tu posais des braises brûlantes sur sa tête. Ta bonté peut lui faire honte et lui faire regretter ce qu’il a fait.

ko.L: 그러나 당신의 원수가 굶주리면 그를 먹이고, 목말라하면 그에게 마실 것을 주십시오. 이렇게 함으로써 당신은 그의 머리 위에 숯불을 쌓을 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 오히려 원수가 굶주리면 먹을 것을 주고, 목말라하면 마실 것을 주십시오. 그렇게 하면 그의 머리 위에 불타는 숯을 쌓아 놓는 것이 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 오히려 원수가 배고파하면 먹을 것을 주십시오. 목말라하면 마실 것을 주십시오. 그렇게 하면 그의 머리 위에 불타는 숯을 쌓는 것과 같을 것입니다. 그런 친절을 받으면 그는 부끄러워하고 뉘우치게 될지도 모릅니다.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu kẻ thù của bạn đói, hãy cho người ấy ăn; nếu người ấy khát, hãy cho người ấy uống; vì làm như vậy, bạn sẽ chất than lửa đỏ trên đầu người ấy.
vi.B: Trái lại, nếu kẻ thù của bạn đói, hãy cho người ấy ăn; nếu người ấy khát, hãy cho người ấy uống. Làm như vậy là bạn chất than hồng lên đầu người ấy.
vi.R: Trái lại, nếu kẻ thù của bạn đói, hãy cho người ấy ăn. Nếu người ấy khát, hãy cho người ấy uống. Khi bạn làm như vậy, điều đó giống như chất than hồng lên đầu người ấy. Lòng tốt của bạn có thể khiến người ấy xấu hổ và hối hận.

decisions.choice: But if
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "if therefore" in place of ἀλλὰ ἐὰν. SBLGNT follows early manuscripts with "but". Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Proverbs 25:21-22
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the old Greek translation of Proverbs 25:21-22 almost word for word, without an introduction. Proverbs adds that the LORD will reward the one who does it.

decisions.choice: heap burning coals on his head: a painful shame that may lead the enemy to change
alternatives: adding to the enemy's punishment at God's judgment
decisions.reason: The picture is of burning pain. Most take it to mean the burning shame an enemy feels when repaid with kindness, which may lead to repentance; this fits verse 21, overcoming evil with good. Others take it as heaping up judgment on an enemy who does not repent, but that sits poorly with verses 14 and 17-19.

decisions.choice: evil: the evil done to you, and evil as a power
decisions.reason: "The evil" is first the wrong an enemy does (verse 17), but Paul speaks of it as a power that can conquer, as he speaks of sin in chapters 5-7. Paying back evil would let it win.

decisions.choice: with good: by means of doing good
decisions.reason: Good is the means of victory: kindness to the enemy, as in verse 20.
